items.title: Steve Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: I began to listen to Ellington records and Basie records and Erskine Hawkins and Fletcher Henderson

ctx.x: It has a great bridge, but the bridge is real composition. The other is pretty lightweight music, although it’s a nice song and it deserves to be a hit. But anyway, every American kid like later they wanted to be Elvis Presley or Mickey Mouse or whoever American kids at one point or another want to be. A lot of us wanted to be Eddie Duchin in those days. And parenthetically I’ve run into maybe 200 guys within a certain age bracket since I did the Goodman movie who told me that when they were little they wanted to…

their called Hyde Park. It was there I met Mel Torme, he was another student, and some other guys who did not go on to become well known but were into jazz, were interested in it and could play it, starting to learn, working with neighborhood dance bands and stuff. And it was there that I got interested in jazz, just listening to records at these kids houses. Before that I had of course heard jazz and enjoyed it. You might say well how could you be hearing jazz and enjoying it without being sort of emotionally…
Oh forget mostly. It was superior.
